name: App Screenshot Creator
tagline: Browser tool for laying out App Store and Google Play screenshot sets with templates, type, and device frames.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a layout tool with store-specific canvas sizes, not a platform. The hard parts are knowing the required pixel dimensions per device class and exporting clean PNGs at exact size, and both are public knowledge plus one rendering library. An agent can produce a local editor with presets, background gradients, headline text, screenshot upload, device frames, and a zip export in a single sitting. What you will not get in one shot is the taste baked into the paid templates or a frame library that stays current with each new iPhone. If you ship one app a year, build it; if you ship screenshots for clients weekly, the polish is worth money.
coreLoopDIY: A local React editor that composites your uploaded screenshots into store-sized canvases with headline text, background, and optional device frame, then exports the whole set as correctly dimensioned PNGs.
requirements: Your own device frame PNGs or SVGs if you want frames
Fonts you are licensed to use
whatYouLose: Curated templates that someone already A/B thought about
A maintained device frame library that tracks new hardware and bezel changes
Store spec updates when Apple or Google quietly changes required dimensions
Bundled commercial-use fonts and background art
Projects that follow you between machines without you syncing a folder
moatNotes: The real asset is the template and frame library, not the canvas code. Everything downstream of that is drawing rectangles.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because screenshot sets are a once-every-few-months chore and nobody wants to rediscover that the 6.9 inch display needs a specific pixel size at 11pm before a release. Paying means opening a tab, dropping in six PNGs, typing six headlines, and being done, with frames and fonts that look deliberate instead of like a Tailwind default. A self-built version matches that on output quality but only after you supply the assets and taste yourself.
notes: Exact export dimensions are the whole job here, so test one upload against a real App Store Connect submission before trusting your build.
prompt:
Build a local-only App Store screenshot layout tool. Empty folder, no accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind. State in Zustand. Persist projects to localStorage. Export with html-to-image and bundle with JSZip + file-saver. No server, no database, no auth.

Data model: a Project has a name, a target preset, and an ordered list of Slides. A Slide has: uploaded screenshot (data URL), headline text, subheadline text, background (solid color or two-stop linear gradient with angle), text color, font family, font size, text position (top or bottom), screenshot scale and vertical offset, and an optional device frame.

Presets, hardcoded in src/presets.ts with a comment linking to the official spec: iPhone 6.9in (1290x2796), iPhone 6.5in (1242x2688), iPad 13in (2064x2752), Android phone (1080x1920), Android tablet (1600x2560). Each preset stores exact export pixel width and height.

Editor UI: left sidebar is a vertical slide list with add, duplicate, delete, and drag to reorder. Center is the live canvas rendered at true preset pixel size inside a container scaled down with CSS transform so it fits the viewport. Right sidebar is the inspector for the selected slide.

Critical: the canvas DOM node must always be laid out at true export pixels; only the wrapper is transformed. Export must temporarily reset the transform, call toPng with pixelRatio 1, and restore it, so output is exactly the preset dimensions. Verify this with a test that checks exported image width and height.

Device frames: read PNG or SVG files from /public/frames at runtime via a frames.json manifest listing filename, display name, and the inset rectangle (x, y, width, height as fractions) where the screenshot should be masked. Ship frames.json with an empty array and a README explaining how to add frames. Do not fabricate or bundle frame art.

Fonts: a small picker over system font stacks plus any font the user loads with a local file input via FontFace. No Google Fonts fetch.

Apply-to-all buttons in the inspector for background, font, text color, and text position, so a six slide set stays consistent.

Export: single slide as PNG or JPG, or whole project as a zip named project-slug.zip with files 01.png, 02.png and so on. Also export and import the project as JSON.

Out of scope: cloud sync, sharing links, collaboration, localized text variants, video previews, direct App Store Connect upload.

Ship a README with run instructions and one worked example: three slides, gradient background, no frames.
